name: can-the-devtools-frontend-be-driven
description:
The remaining DevTools checks need DevTools' OWN frontend driven - the dock-side buttons, the divider, detach. Harness key and click actions cannot reach those, so a human would have to verify them. The eval capability makes it worth one attempt.

This asks the narrow question first: can a scenario reach the DevTools frontend document at all? If /devtools appears as a target and its DOM reads back, the dock buttons are reachable and those criteria become automatable. If it does not, that is a definite answer rather than an assumption, and the human-verification recommendation stands on evidence.

actions.note: let the space and its single tab render
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot; without this the keystroke lands in Finder (traffic-routing learned this the hard way)
open DevTools on the active tab
DevTools frontend is a full WebContents load - generous on purpose, the dock VLOG only fires once UpdateDockedDevtoolsForPane runs with a non-null GetInTabWebContents
the whole question: does a devtools:// target answer at all

actions.expression: (() => { const seen = []; const walk = (root, depth) => { if (depth > 6) return; for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('*')) {   if (el.shadowRoot) walk(el.shadowRoot, depth + 1);   const t = el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('aria-label');   if (t) seen.push(t); } }; walk(document, 0); return String(seen.length); })()
actions.note: counts labelled controls across the shadow trees. DevTools builds its UI in shadow roots, so a light-DOM query finds nothing even when the frontend is fully loaded - which is why the first attempt read 0.

actions.expression: (() => { const hits = []; const walk = (root, depth) => { if (depth > 8) return; for (const el of root.querySelectorAll('*')) {   if (el.shadowRoot) walk(el.shadowRoot, depth + 1);   const l = (el.getAttribute && el.getAttribute('aria-label')) || '';   if (/dock|customize|control|more option/i.test(l)) hits.push(l); } }; walk(document, 0); return hits.join(' | ') || 'none'; })()
actions.note: Chrome puts Dock side behind the 'Customize and control DevTools' menu rather than on the toolbar, so this looks for the menu button too - that is the control a scenario would press first.

assertions.label: devtools-docked
assertions.note: The pane resolved a docked DevTools WebContents - the sole writer of this state
still ONE standard window: a detached DevTools would add a second, so this is what proves 'docked' rather than merely 'opened'
a reachable, loaded frontend document. BLIND here means no devtools target is exposed, which answers the question the other way.
